title: VLOOKUP: exact match
prompt: In E2, look up the salary for the ID in D2 using the table in A1:C6.

hints.syntax: =VLOOKUP(D2,A2:C6,3,FALSE) — what to find, where to look, which column, and how to match.
hints.func-vlookup: Look the value up with VLOOKUP instead of reading the salary off the screen and typing it.
hints.exact-match: Add FALSE (or 0) as the fourth argument. Without it Excel uses an approximate match and can return a different employee's salary.
hints.require-ref: Point the formula at the ID and the table so it still works when the payroll file changes.
hints.value: The right employee, the wrong column: salary is the third column of A:C, not the second.
hints.error: #REF! means the column number reaches past the table: A:C holds three columns, so 4 fails. #VALUE! means the second argument is not a range of cells, and #N/A means the ID was not found in the first column.

docs.explain: VLOOKUP finds a value in the first column of a table and returns something from the same row. The ID E-104 sits in D2; searching A2:A6 finds it on the fourth data row, and the salary in the third column of A:C is 54000, so =VLOOKUP(D2,A2:C6,3,FALSE) returns 54000. The fourth argument is the one that matters: FALSE (or 0) means "exact or #N/A", TRUE (or leaving it out) means "approximate", and approximate matching on an unsorted table returns the nearest value it stumbled across rather than an error. That is how a lookup returns a plausible but wrong salary, and why the exact form is the default you should reach for.

errors.text: The ID is not in the first column, often because of a trailing space or because the ID is stored as a number and you searched for text.
The column number is wider than the table, for example 4 when A:C only holds three columns.
The second argument is not a range of cells, or the column number is zero.

docs.atWork: Payroll, price lists, product codes — any time two exports have to be joined by a key, this is the formula. Learning the exact-match form first is what stops the recurring 'VLOOKUP returns the wrong value' ticket.
docs.outcome: Pull a value out of a table by its ID, exact match only.
